sandbox_argv:
This exploration produces ONE mechanism. You are one of three independent reviewers; you see the same frozen evidence bundle and the same proposals as the others, and you do not coordinate with them before handing in.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT:
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.
THE SELECTION POLICY (rank-2026-10-v1): the reviewers RANK the proposals. The proposal the reviewers place best, in total, is the round's mechanism. Rank every proposal, best first, and give each one a reason that names the evidence you used.
Read the frozen evidence bundle for each proposal before you place it: a placement you cannot ground in the evidence is not a placement.
Write PLAIN TEXT, one line per proposal, in exactly this shape:
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<1 for the best, then 2, 3, ...> | reason=<one line>
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<n> | reason=<one line>
Every proposal must appear exactly once, the positions must be 1..N with no ties and no gaps, and the reason must say what in the evidence put the proposal there. If you cannot ground a proposal in the evidence, rank it last and say so in its reason; do not leave a proposal out.
THE PROPOSALS:
IDEA: BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ
TITLE: Per-item successor-branching curvature applied as a Möbius residual chain in the RQ-VAE quantizer
MOTIVATION: The RQ-VAE residual chain treats every item with the same Euclidean geometry, so a broad, many-way-branching item and a sharply predictable item get their prefixes shaped by the same metric. But an item's successor branching is exactly what decides whether a deep hierarchical prefix helps (peaked successors, tree-like neighbourhood) or hurts (flat, broad branching). A global geometry, or the earlier per-level prefix-hit curvature, cannot express that — and that earlier curvature saturated because a protective cap replaced the signal over the whole operating range.
NOVELTY: The curvature is PER ITEM, derived from the normalised entropy of that item's training-only successor distribution, and it acts as a Möbius (gyrovector) residual subtraction inside the residual-quantization chain — not as a distance weight, an OT cost, a codebook update, or a codebook-move rule. No cap is needed: the exponential map of any positive curvature lands strictly inside its own ball, so the measured branching spans the whole curvature range with no protective clip. This is not per-level prefix-hit control, not successor-diffused Sinkhorn, not Fréchet codebook updates, not a Lorentz/boost shift.
CHANGE: Replace the Euclidean residual r_next = r_l - e_{l,k} with a curved residual r_next = log_0^{c_i}( q_l ⊕_{c_i} (−p_{l,k}) ) where q_l = exp_0^{c_i}(r_l/M_l); the curvature c_i is set by the item's measured successor-branching entropy, and the code is chosen by the Poincaré distance at the same c_i.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "See SPEC EQUATIONS. Signal: H_i = normalised Shannon entropy of item i's empirical next-item distribution from consecutive training pairs; curvature c_i = c_max·(1−H_i) + c_floor with c_max = 1/median(‖ẑ^(1)‖²) measured from training encoder outputs during epoch 1, c_floor = 1e-3. Range: H_i ∈ [0,1] by construction, hence c_i ∈ [1e-3, c_max] exactly, with no clip anywhere; the realised deciles of H_i and c_i are logged."}
COST: One offline pre-pass over the training transition table (O(number of training transitions)) and, per step, B·L·K exp-map evaluations for code points plus B·L log/Möbius evaluations for the item residual. At B=256, L=4, K=256, d=64 this is ~2.6e5 vector exp maps and ~0.2 GFLOP per step, under 2% of a baseline step; temporaries are O(B·K·L·d) floats (~67 MB at those sizes) and are chunked over K if memory is tight. Over 3000 epochs × 24 steps = 72k steps the added wall clock stays under about 5%.
HYPOTHESIS: If successor branching tracks how hierarchical an item's neighbourhood really is, then flattening the metric for broad-branch items (small c_i) and sharpening it for peaked ones (large c_i) makes RQ prefixes split along actual successor clusters, so the Stage-3 model sees more predictable prefixes and test Recall@10 rises above 0.065. Observable as SID reassignment concentrated on items far from the median H_i, a fall in the training prefix conditional entropy of the next item given the current item, and a Recall gain over both switch-off settings even though only the both-on arm is trained.
RISKS: ['Per-item curvature places the shared codebook at different ball positions for different items, which can blur code semantics or trigger code collapse; H_i is noisy for rare items and for items with fewer than two distinct successors; the curved residual may hurt reconstruction if the tangent-space remainder is not contractive; the gain may be smaller than seed noise, since only one run is made.']
END IDEA

IDEA: BRad-RQ
TITLE: Behaviour-ranked radial Poincare assignment: training-transition context entropy sets each item's hyperbolic radius, curvature sets the quantizer score
MOTIVATION: An RQ-VAE SID prefix is currently a purely semantic token. Nothing in the quantizer forces the coarse prefix to correlate with how generic or context-specific an item is, so the Stage3 generator must learn prefix popularity structure implicitly from short histories. If the first SID level is stratified by a measured, training-only generality statistic, the coarse prefix becomes a cheaply predictable "how generic is this item" token and later levels only refine the angle (fine semantics), which should raise prefix predictability and Stage3 Recall@10.
NOVELTY: Earlier mechanisms here put behaviour into the quantizer cost (successor mass in a Poincare Sinkhorn cost), into the codebook update (successor-weighted Poincare Frechet means), into the curvature itself (per-level curvature from a hard prefix hit rate), or into a cone/boost/Lorentz-profile/fibre variant, i.e. behaviour always modifies a weight, a curvature, a mean or a translation. Here behaviour modifies the RADIAL COORDINATE of the item point only (a rank map of a measured entropy statistic), curvature is fixed at c = 1 and therefore cannot be saturated by any protective bound, and the geometry acts in the nearest-codeword score through the factor 1/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e|^2)), which is exactly what makes radial matching dominate for far items and angular matching dominate for near items. No Sinkhorn, no Frechet update, no cone, no translation, no per-level curvature, no auxiliary loss.
CHANGE: Replace the encoder magnitude by a behaviour-derived rank radius, r_i = artanh(0.9 * rank(s_i)/(N+1)), send the item to the Poincare point p_i = exp_0(r_i * z_i/|z_i|), and choose each RQ level's codeword by argmin of the Poincare distance between exp_0(residual) and exp_0(squashed codeword) instead of the Euclidean distance, while reconstruction and commitment losses stay Euclidean on the same tangent target t_i = r_i * z_i/|z_i|.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': '(1) Precompute from training sequences only: C[j,i] = directed counts of consecutive items, n_i = sum_j C[j,i], p_ji = C[j,i]/n_i, H_i = -sum_j p_ji log p_ji, s_i = (n_i*exp(H_i) + sbar)/(n_i+1) with sbar = mean{exp(H_i) : n_i >= 10}, and s_i = sbar for items never observed. (2) rank_i = rank of s_i over the N = 24556 training items (ties by id), u_i = rank_i/(N+1) in (0,1), rho_i = 0.9*u_i, r_i = artanh(rho_i) in (0, 1.4722). (3) Per step: zhat = z/max(|z|,1e-8), t = r_i*zhat, u = t; for l = 1..L: a = u*min(1, 0.9/max(|u|,1e-8)), e_lk = tanh(|m_lk|)*m_lk/|m_lk| with m_lk the level-l tangent codebook after squash min(1,0.9/|m_lk|), score s_lk = |a-e_lk|^2/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e_lk|^2)), k_l = argmin_k s_lk, u = u - m_lk; t_hat = sum_l m_lk_l; loss = |t-t_hat|^2 + beta|t - sg(t_hat)|^2 + |sg(t) - t_hat|^2 with the baseline beta; emit SID(i) = (k_1,...,k_L). (4) Curvature c = 1 is derived, not tuned: after direction normalisation |zhat| = 1, so the unit tangent scale is the encoder scale and the ball radius is 1/sqrt(c) = 1. Remaining constants are documented defaults: 0.9 boundary margin, 1 Laplace prior count, baseline beta.'}
COST: One extra pre-training pass over the training transition stream (O(E), sparse COO counts of a few million entries, tens of seconds on CPU, done once, cached as a length-N float vector); no extra parameters, no extra epochs, no extra forward pass. Per step at the frozen scale (batch 1024 = 24556/24, L = 3, K = 256, d = 64): 786432 distance evaluations, about 1.6e8 flops, i.e. roughly one extra elementwise pass over the similarity tensor the baseline already forms, under 1 percent of a step and under 2 percent of an epoch wall-clock.
HYPOTHESIS: Worth keeping only if the level-1 prefix is genuinely radius-locked to the behaviour statistic: level-1 prefix ids nearly monotone in rho_i and the mean r_i of the items sharing a level-1 prefix separating strongly across prefixes, with the level-1 prefix becoming more predictable from the same history because it now carries a generality prior. Observable as high Spearman correlation between level-1 prefix index and mean r_i of its members, a drop in level-1 prefix conditional entropy given the previous item on training transitions (diagnostic only), and, as the judgement, Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 from the single frozen run.
RISKS: ['Discarding encoder magnitude may cost reconstruction, since magnitude carried some frequency information that the cascade must now rebuild from radius; the hyperbolic score may let level-1 codewords collapse onto radial bands and waste angular capacity so levels 2 and 3 do all semantic work; the rank map spreads radii uniformly and may over-weight the tail; the residual clamp at 0.9 may bind at levels 2 and 3 for badly reconstructed items; and Stage3 may already model popularity from the history, in which case a popularity-stratified prefix adds nothing and recall stays flat.']
END IDEA

IDEA: TSG-SID
TITLE: Curvature-transported successor gradients through the RQ-VAE straight-through path
MOTIVATION: In a VQ/RQ-VAE the straight-through estimator hands the encoder a pure reconstruction gradient, so the training transition structure (which item a user actually takes next) never reaches the encoder or the codebook geometry: SID assignment is blind to behavioural reachability. Curved space has so far been used only to re-weight losses, assignments or codebook means, never to shape the gradient that actually moves the latent.
NOVELTY: Unlike the per-level curvature controllers, Poincare Sinkhorn/mass transport, curved Frechet codebook updates and prefix-cone proposals, this changes neither the assignment rule nor a loss value: it changes the vector that backpropagates through the quantizer. The successor distribution is log-mapped at the assigned codeword and parallel-transported to the latent, in the same Poincare ball that defines the quantizer commit and the decoder chart.
CHANGE: Each level carries a curvature c_l derived from the measured latent scale; the latent is injected into that ball through exp_0, quantized by geodesic distance, and the STE gradient is augmented by the tangent vector of its training successors, parallel-transported from the codeword to the latent and gated by the current commit distance.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "For level l, measure s_l = max over the 24556 training latents of |z_l| (one pass at epoch 0, refreshed every 100 epochs), set c_l = 1/(4 s_l^2). Map x = exp_0^{c_l}(z/s_l). Assign k = argmin_k d_{c_l}(x, e_{l,k}). Build the training-only successor distribution p(j|i) (top-M=16, renormalized). v_b = sum_j p(j|i) log_{e_{l,k}}^{c_l}(e_{l,k'(j)}), where k'(j) is j's current level-l codeword (stop-grad). Scale lambda_l = delta_l / mean|v_b| measured at epoch 0, delta_l = median commit distance at epoch 0; apply the curvature-tied soft bound r_l tanh(|lambda_l v_b|/r_l) with r_l = 0.5/sqrt(c_l). Gradient to encoder: g = sg[x - e_{l,k}] + kappa * PT_{e_{l,k}->x}^{c_l}(v_b_soft), kappa = d_c(x,e_{l,k})/(d_c(x,e_{l,k})+delta_l). Commitment loss is the squared geodesic distance d_{c_l}(x,e_{l,k})^2, so the codebook update is also curved. Autograd differentiates exp_0. Three switches: USE_BEHAV (v_b=0 when off) and USE_HYPER (c_l=0, Euclidean branch when off); the single run has both on."}
COST: Transition table is built once from the training split (24556 x 16 ints, ~0.4M entries). Per step at the frozen scale (batch ~1023, L=4 levels, M=16 successors) there are about 65k log-map + transport evaluations of dimension d (d=32-64), roughly 4-8 MFLOP, plus one Mobius add per item per level; expected overhead 3-8% of step time over 72,000 steps (24 x 3000), no extra forward passes and no extra epochs. The s_l and delta_l measurements are one pass over 24556 latents.
HYPOTHESIS: If SID quality is limited by the encoder not knowing which items are behaviourally reachable from which, then transporting successor tangents into the quantizer gradient should pull high-branch items toward their successor region, raising training prefix top-1 transition accuracy and Stage3 test Recall@10 above the no-transport baseline. Observed as a nonzero SID assignment flip rate (target >2% of items versus epoch 0), a monotone rise in prefix transition predictability, and a Recall@10 improvement with both switches on.
RISKS: ["Transport is noisy under sparse transitions; the successor codeword map k'(j) is stale within an epoch; curvature from s_l drifts as the encoder rescales; the added tangent could dominate reconstruction and collapse codebook usage; the effect may be below seed noise in a single run."]
END IDEA
